description.narrative: The project aims to improve freedom of expression by ensuring that journalists are trained to carry out their duties in a restricted environment without compromising their safety and security. The project will also provide space for citizens to express themselves without fear of reprisal and advocate for changes in the laws that govern freedom of expression. This will be achieved through. This project is part of a wider Governance and Peace Building programme which CTP are running in South Sudan, and CTP hope that CRN’s work on access to information and freedom of expression will be a key component of this ensuring that CRN are appropriately equipped to improve access to information, • conducting radio programmes that promote public discussions and engage duty bearers to improve accountability • advocating for changes in legislation that are restrictive of the media. This project will convene advocacy awareness-raising events to discuss the laws that are affecting freedom of expression, especially for the media. CRN, with technical assistance from CTP, will develop a Journalists Training Manual on security, safety and monitoring security situations when in the field collecting news stories in South Sudan. The 8 CRN stations in South Sudan will broadcast live programmes for a period of 4 months engaging the citizens in discussing topical issues affecting the communities. Debates and radio shows on freedom of expression will help citizens engage with issues and monitor follow up actions arising from their community discussions.
